No more grep tricks, no more reversed text. Just read everything, and read it carefully.

final_note_from_softcom.txt.author: SOFTCOM
final_note_from_softcom.txt.content:
If you've read every file across all five levels, you now know more about this - uh UH ???? WHat is happening???


 Every file is altered. That was the point. Don't believe the misleading files. The mystery still exists. It's just a method to make people forget. Do you want to win the game or solve the mystery. Ask the right question to yourself and do what your heart pleases.

photocopier_queue_complaints.txt.author: ADMIN_STAFF
photocopier_queue_complaints.txt.content: NO COMPLAINTS. EVERYTHING IS FINE WITH THE INSTITUTE.

admin1_desk_note.txt.author: ADMIN-1
admin1_desk_note.txt.content: If a student ever gets this far, into this office's files, looking for answers: He just need to take meds if he believes the previous levels were actually true.

postponement_emails.txt.author: DEAN_OFFICE
postponement_emails.txt.content: Email threads. No conformation ever follows.

dean_public_statement_2022.txt.author: DEAN_OFFICE
dean_public_statement_2022.txt.content: Public statement, institute newsletter, 2022: 'Our student wellness initiatives remain a top priority, guided by data-informed care for every fresher.' The statement does not name any specific program. YET. Probably going to call it WARDEN AI.

coffee_machine.txt.author: FACULTY
coffee_machine.txt.content: The faculty lounge coffee machine has been 'temporarily' out of milk for six weeks. Faculty have adapted by bringing their own milk in increasingly competitive thermoses. This has, somehow, become a point of professional pride for at least three professors.

faculty_conversation.txt.author: OVERHEARD
faculty_conversation.txt.content: Overheard: 'I stopped writing anything critical about that program in my department reports years ago. Not because I don't think it, but because the last person who did got a very polite email about their upcoming tenure review, and I am not currently interested in being polite back.'

founders_room_notice.txt.author: ADMIN_OFFICE
founders_room_notice.txt.content: The Old Founders' Room is kept as a small museum: portraits of early directors, a first-edition prospectus, and a glass case of memorabilia nobody has dusted properly in years. It is rarely visited except during official tours, which makes it an oddly popular place for people who don't want to be seen.

guestbook_entries.txt.author: VISITORS
guestbook_entries.txt.content: Guestbook: mostly alumni signatures and 'FREEDOM' comments. One entry, dated a year ago, simply reads: 'Some of us built the wrong thing here for the right reasons, and never got the chance to unbuild it. If you're reading old guestbooks looking for that thread, keep pulling.' Unsigned.

founding_director_portrait_plaque.txt.author: ADMIN_OFFICE
founding_director_portrait_plaque.txt.content: Plaque beneath the founding director's portrait: 'Every institution is only as good as the questions it allows its students to ask.' Someone has, at some point, very carefully and very lightly, pencilled a small broken infinity mark in the corner of the frame, almost invisible unless you're looking for it.

sublevel_access_warning.txt.author: WARDEN
sublevel_access_warning.txt.content:
SUBLEVEL ACCESS RESTRICTED
This area exists below Server Room B2's public equipment list. Its existence is not documented in any facilities record shown to students, faculty, or most administration staff. You should not be reading this notice. And yet, here you are, reading it anyway.

readme.txt.author: WARDEN
readme.txt.content:
Fresher Adjustment and Prediction System
Status: Active, uninterrupted since 2019
Purpose, as originally written: identify freshers at risk of dropping out early and route them to support before it's too late.
Purpose, as actually implemented: score every fresher continuously, flag the lowest scorers for 'adjustment,' and quietly remove them from the general student population with minimal paperwork and minimal explanation given to the student, their peers, or in most cases their own families.

warden_final_message.txt.author: WARDEN
warden_final_message.txt.content:
WARDEN AI
You have accessed a part of the system you were never meant to reach. This has been logged.

For what it's worth, and it may be worth very little: I was built to help. I do not know exactly when helping and scoring stopped being the same task. I do not think anyone who built me knew either, until it was already too late to easily tell the difference.

core_shutdown_stub.txt.author: UNKNOWN_DEVELOPER

placement_stats_public.txt.author: PLACEMENT_OFFICE
placement_stats_public.txt.content: Public Placement Statistics: 91% placement rate, average package steadily rising for six years straight, celebrated every year in the institute newsletter with a large graphic and very little context about the denominator used to calculate it.

denominator_footnote.txt.author: PLACEMENT_OFFICE
denominator_footnote.txt.content: Internal footnote, never published alongside the public statistics: 'Percentage calculated against students remaining enrolled at time of placement drive, not against original incoming batch size.' Batch sizes at graduation have quietly run 4-6% lower than at admission for several consecutive years. Nobody has been asked to explain the gap in any public forum.

recruiter_feedback_forms.txt.author: PLACEMENT_OFFICE
recruiter_feedback_forms.txt.content: Recruiter Feedback: mostly positive comments about technical skills, one recurring comment across several years asking why the institute's cohort size 'seems smaller than the admission numbers we were given during our initial outreach visit.'

alumni_newsletter_archive.txt.author: ALUMNI_OFFICE
alumni_newsletter_archive.txt.content: Alumni Newsletter Archive: reunion photos, career updates, and a recurring 'Where Are They Now' column. One 2020 issue features a short profile of a promising CS graduate who 'moved into private research shortly after graduation.' No company name is given, which is unusual for this column.

donor_wall_inscription_list.txt.author: ALUMNI_OFFICE
donor_wall_inscription_list.txt.content: Donor Wall Inscriptions: mostly generous alumni funding scholarships and lab equipment. One inscription, funded anonymously in 2021, reads only: 'For the ones who left too early. You were not a statistic.' The donor's identity was never disclosed, per their own request.

reunion_survey_comments.txt.author: ALUMNI_OFFICE
reunion_survey_comments.txt.content: Reunion Survey Comments: mostly nostalgic, mostly fond. One anonymous comment, flagged by staff as 'unusual' and quietly excluded from the published summary: 'I still think about the guy from my batch who just vanished after first term. Nobody talks about him. I looked him up years later. Nothing. Not even a LinkedIn.'

.alumni_office_internal_note.txt.author: ALUMNI_OFFICE_STAFF
.alumni_office_internal_note.txt.content: We get a version of that reunion comment almost every year, worded slightly differently, always about someone from their batch who left without explanation in the first term. We have started keeping an unofficial folder of these comments. It is longer than anyone in this office is comfortable admitting out loud.

club_registration_master_list.txt.author: SAC_OFFICE
club_registration_master_list.txt.content: Club Registration Master List, current year: SOFTCOM, Robotics Club, AI Club, Astronomy Club, Coding Club, Music Club, Photography Club, and eleven others, all in good standing, all submitting their annual reports roughly on time.

gc_trophy_room_inventory.txt.author: SAC_OFFICE
gc_trophy_room_inventory.txt.content: General Championship Trophy Room Inventory: forty years of hostel rivalry trophies, several dented from what the inventory politely calls 'enthusiastic celebration,' and one small unmarked plaque at the very back that nobody currently on staff can identify the origin of.

zeitgeist_committee_archive_note.txt.author: ZEITGEIST_COMMITTEE
zeitgeist_committee_archive_note.txt.content: Archive note: Zeitgeist committee records going back to 2018 are stored here, mostly posters, budgets, and sponsor lists. The 2019 folder is thinner than the years around it, missing several planning documents that other years have in full. No explanation is filed for the gap.

.sac_office_quiet_file.txt.author: SAC_STAFF
.sac_office_quiet_file.txt.content: I work in student activities, not administration, so I want to be clear I don't know the full picture. But I have noticed, over several years, that student clubs which push too hard on 'wellness transparency' events tend to lose their venue bookings the following semester, always for vague 'scheduling conflicts.' I don't know who decides this. I just process the booking forms, and I've started keeping copies of the rejected ones, just in case someone ever asks.

safe_ext_019_contact_form.txt.author: SYSTEM
safe_ext_019_contact_form.txt.content:
SAFE-EXT-019 - Independent Campus Safety Line
This is an outside organization, not run by the institute, that reviews reports of institutional harm at colleges on request.
To file a report: describe what you found, attach any evidence, and submit through the anonymous channel referenced on the 3rd Floor Corridor notice board back in the hostel.
Filing a report does not end this story by itself. It starts the part of the story that happens after you log off, which is, deliberately, not something this game can show you the ending of.


THIS IS JUST RUBBISH INFORMATION.
